"""Parse flexible, human-written date expressions into concrete dates."""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from datetime import date, datetime

import dateparser
from dateutil.relativedelta import FR, MO, SA, SU, TH, TU, WE, relativedelta

WEEKDAYS = {
    "monday": MO, "tuesday": TU, "wednesday": WE, "thursday": TH,
    "friday": FR, "saturday": SA, "sunday": SU,
}
ORDINALS = {
    "first": 1, "1st": 1, "second": 2, "2nd": 2, "third": 3, "3rd": 3,
    "fourth": 4, "4th": 4, "fifth": 5, "5th": 5, "last": -1,
}
MONTHS = {
    name: i
    for i, name in enumerate(
        ["january", "february", "march", "april", "may", "june", "july",
         "august", "september", "october", "november", "december"],
        start=1,
    )
}

# "the first Monday of next month", "last friday in this month",
# "2nd tuesday of march", "third thursday of november 2027"
_NTH_WEEKDAY = re.compile(
    rf"^(?:the\s+)?(?P<ord>{'|'.join(ORDINALS)})\s+"
    rf"(?P<wd>{'|'.join(WEEKDAYS)})\s+(?:of|in)\s+(?P<month>.+)$",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)


class DateParseError(ValueError):
    """Raised when an expression cannot be interpreted as a date."""


def nth_weekday(year: int, month: int, n: int, weekday: str) -> date:
    """Return the nth (1-5, or -1 for last) given weekday of a month."""
    wd = WEEKDAYS[weekday.lower()]
    first = date(year, month, 1)
    if n == -1:
        result = first + relativedelta(day=31, weekday=wd(-1))
    else:
        result = first + relativedelta(weekday=wd(n))
    if result.month != month:
        raise DateParseError(f"{year}-{month:02d} has no {n}th {weekday}")
    return result


def _resolve_month(text: str, today: date) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """Resolve 'next month', 'this month', 'last month', 'march', 'march 2027'."""
    text = text.strip().lower()
    relative = {"this month": 0, "next month": 1, "last month": -1, "previous month": -1}
    if text in relative:
        target = today + relativedelta(months=relative[text])
        return target.year, target.month

    match = re.fullmatch(r"(?:next\s+)?([a-z]+)(?:\s+(\d{4}))?", text)
    if match and match.group(1) in MONTHS:
        month = MONTHS[match.group(1)]
        if match.group(2):
            return int(match.group(2)), month
        # A bare month name means its next occurrence (including the current month).
        year = today.year if month >= today.month else today.year + 1
        if text.startswith("next ") and month == today.month:
            year += 1
        return year, month

    raise DateParseError(f"Unrecognised month expression: {text!r}")


def parse_date(text: str, today: date | None = None) -> date:
    """Parse a human-written date expression relative to ``today``.

    Handles "Nth weekday of <month>" phrases directly and delegates everything
    else ("tomorrow", "in 3 weeks", "next friday", "2026-12-25", ...) to dateparser.
    """
    today = today or date.today()
    text = text.strip()

    if match := _NTH_WEEKDAY.match(text):
        year, month = _resolve_month(match["month"], today)
        return nth_weekday(year, month, ORDINALS[match["ord"].lower()], match["wd"])

    parsed = dateparser.parse(
        text,
        settings={
            "RELATIVE_BASE": datetime.combine(today, datetime.min.time()),
            "PREFER_DATES_FROM": "future",
        },
    )
    if parsed is None:
        raise DateParseError(f"Could not parse date: {text!r}")
    return parsed.date()
EOF

"""Parse flexible, human-written date strings."""

import argparse
from datetime import date

from datewise.parsing import DateParseError, nth_weekday, parse_date

__all__ = ["DateParseError", "nth_weekday", "parse_date", "main"]


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Resolve a human-written date expression.")
    parser.add_argument("expression", nargs="+", help='e.g. "the first Monday of next month"')
    parser.add_argument("--today", type=date.fromisoformat, help="reference date (YYYY-MM-DD)")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    try:
        result = parse_date(" ".join(args.expression), today=args.today)
    except DateParseError as exc:
        parser.exit(1, f"error: {exc}\n")
    print(f"{result.isoformat()} ({result:%A})")
EOF

from datetime import date

import pytest

from datewise import DateParseError, nth_weekday, parse_date

TODAY = date(2026, 10, 2)  # a Friday


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("text", "expected"),
    [
        ("the first Monday of next month", date(2026, 11, 2)),
        ("first monday of this month", date(2026, 10, 5)),
        ("last Friday of next month", date(2026, 11, 27)),
        ("2nd Tuesday in March", date(2027, 3, 9)),
        ("third Thursday of November 2027", date(2027, 11, 18)),
        ("the 4th thursday of november", date(2026, 11, 26)),
    ],
)
def test_nth_weekday_phrases(text, expected):
    assert parse_date(text, today=TODAY) == expected


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("text", "expected"),
    [
        ("tomorrow", date(2026, 10, 3)),
        ("in 3 days", date(2026, 10, 5)),
        ("2 weeks ago", date(2026, 9, 18)),
        ("2026-12-25", date(2026, 12, 25)),
        ("March 5, 2027", date(2027, 3, 5)),
    ],
)
def test_delegated_to_dateparser(text, expected):
    assert parse_date(text, today=TODAY) == expected


def test_fifth_weekday_that_does_not_exist():
    with pytest.raises(DateParseError):
        nth_weekday(2026, 2, 5, "monday")


def test_garbage_raises():
    with pytest.raises(DateParseError):
        parse_date("not a date at all", today=TODAY)

"""Parse flexible, human-written date expressions into concrete dates."""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from datetime import date, datetime

import dateparser
from dateutil.relativedelta import FR, MO, SA, SU, TH, TU, WE, relativedelta

WEEKDAYS = {
    "monday": MO, "tuesday": TU, "wednesday": WE, "thursday": TH,
    "friday": FR, "saturday": SA, "sunday": SU,
}
ORDINALS = {
    "first": 1, "1st": 1, "second": 2, "2nd": 2, "third": 3, "3rd": 3,
    "fourth": 4, "4th": 4, "fifth": 5, "5th": 5, "last": -1,
}
MONTHS = {
    name: i
    for i, name in enumerate(
        ["january", "february", "march", "april", "may", "june", "july",
         "august", "september", "october", "november", "december"],
        start=1,
    )
}

# "the first Monday of next month", "last friday in this month",
# "2nd tuesday of march", "third thursday of november 2027"
_NTH_WEEKDAY = re.compile(
    rf"^(?:the\s+)?(?P<ord>{'|'.join(ORDINALS)})\s+"
    rf"(?P<wd>{'|'.join(WEEKDAYS)})\s+(?:of|in)\s+(?P<month>.+)$",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)


class DateParseError(ValueError):
    """Raised when an expression cannot be interpreted as a date."""


def nth_weekday(year: int, month: int, n: int, weekday: str) -> date:
    """Return the nth (1-5, or -1 for last) given weekday of a month."""
    wd = WEEKDAYS[weekday.lower()]
    first = date(year, month, 1)
    if n == -1:
        result = first + relativedelta(day=31, weekday=wd(-1))
    else:
        result = first + relativedelta(weekday=wd(n))
    if result.month != month:
        raise DateParseError(f"{year}-{month:02d} has no {n}th {weekday}")
    return result


def _resolve_month(text: str, today: date) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """Resolve 'next month', 'this month', 'last month', 'march', 'march 2027'."""
    text = text.strip().lower()
    relative = {"this month": 0, "next month": 1, "last month": -1, "previous month": -1}
    if text in relative:
        target = today + relativedelta(months=relative[text])
        return target.year, target.month

    match = re.fullmatch(r"(?:next\s+)?([a-z]+)(?:\s+(\d{4}))?", text)
    if match and match.group(1) in MONTHS:
        month = MONTHS[match.group(1)]
        if match.group(2):
            return int(match.group(2)), month
        # A bare month name means its next occurrence (including the current month).
        year = today.year if month >= today.month else today.year + 1
        if text.startswith("next ") and month == today.month:
            year += 1
        return year, month

    raise DateParseError(f"Unrecognised month expression: {text!r}")

    """Parse a human-written date expression relative to ``today``.

    Handles "Nth weekday of <month>" phrases directly and delegates everything
    else ("tomorrow", "in 3 weeks", "next friday", "2026-12-25", ...) to dateparser.

            "RELATIVE_BASE": datetime.combine(today, datetime.min.time()),
            "PREFER_DATES_FROM": "future",
